title: streaming-envelope-desynchronization-causing-misattributed-tool-output-across-proxies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported that, during streaming function/tool calls, outputs from one invocation were being attributed to a different function call or duplicated. Reports span hosted API, Dedicated gateways, and VPC/private proxy setups. Symptoms: wrong tool selected by the router, duplicate external API invocations, and malformed structured JSON returned to callers. This appears tied to proxy-level re-chunking and our streaming envelope assumptions combined with a race around KV-cache correlation IDs.
customer_reports: Customer A (ecom-analytics) escalated 2026-02-27: observed duplicate webhook calls and mismatch in tool response fields for batched streaming requests sent through their private proxy.
Customer B (fin-platform) reported 2026-02-28: function call B returned output from function A when requests routed through a Dedicated gateway in eu-west-1 during peak load.
Support ticket: #SUP-11472: live logs show repeated 'no-correlation' parser warnings around the time of proxy reconnects.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy two simple function/tool endpoints: /label and /summarize. Both return small JSON payloads and are invoked in rapid succession from a single streaming session.

2) Send a streaming request that triggers sequential tool calls (tool A then tool B) and enable a TCP proxy that buffers writes and replays on reconnect (use 'tc qdisc' to create pause across TLS record boundaries).
3) Introduce artificial network pause between TLS records (200-400ms) so the proxy flushes fragments in different-sized chunks.
4) Observe parser logs: look for mismatched correlation ids, duplicate tool invocations logged in external systems, and JSON envelopes that contain mixed metadata headers + payload.

Minimal harness snippet (python):

import socket, ssl
# open streaming websocket-like connection -> send toolcall frames -> simulate pause by waiting between sends
investigation_summary: Initial triage: parser correlates tool responses to invocation sessions using in-band metadata frames that assume chunk boundaries are preserved end-to-end. In several customer traces we found that the edge proxy re-chunked the stream: header/meta fragments were coalesced with the subsequent payload from a different tool invocation. Correlation IDs are attached in a small header frame; when fragments are merged or split at the proxy, downstream parser sometimes associates header with the wrong payload. Additionally, a race in our KV-cache name resolution caused a short window where the correlation id mapping could be evicted and then reassigned to a concurrent invocation, amplifying misattribution.
logs_and_evidence:
2026-02-27T18:12:32Z customer-A trace: seq=2144 header={invocation:152} payload={tool:label}
-- header fragment shows invocation:152 but payload belonged to invocation:153
Parser warning: 'correlation-mismatch' logged 68 times across 3 customers between 2026-02-27 and 2026-03-01.
Edge proxy capture: TCP segments show TLS records split at non-deterministic boundaries resulting in application-level frame boundary changes.
root_cause: Assumption in streaming transport: we relied on the proxy preserving application frame boundaries (one header frame -> one payload frame). Real-world proxies (and TLS record boundaries) can split or coalesce frames. Without explicit, in-band sequencing or length-prefixing at the application layer, our parser can pair headers and payloads incorrectly when buffering/re-chunking happens. The KV-cache eviction race increased the window where an invocation id could be reused, causing misattribution and duplicate external calls.
proposed_fix: 1) Add sequence numbers and explicit length-prefixed envelopes to all streaming tool/function frames (runtime change). Parser must reassemble using seq numbers and drop mismatched frames rather than trusting chunk boundaries.

2) Short-term mitigation: introduce runtime toggle 'streaming.envelope_v2' that forces the runtime to insert explicit framing for sessions passing through known proxies (enable by default for Dedicated/VPC).
3) Fix KV-cache eviction: extend TTL for live invocation correlation entries and perform CAS checks before reusing ids.
4) Add e2e tests that simulate proxy re-chunking and TLS record splits, and add regression asserts for correlation mismatch counts.
timeline: 2026-02-27: First customer escalates to support. Initial reproducible trace captured.
2026-02-28: Engineering triage assigned to runtime-stability. Reproduced locally with tc qdisc harness.
2026-03-02: Root cause hypothesized: framing assumption + KV-cache race. PoC framing patch created.
2026-03-05: Hotfix toggle implemented and rolled to Dedicated gateway fleet behind feature flag for two customers; observed elimination of duplicates on test traffic.
2026-03-09: PR opened for sequence-number envelope and parser reassembly (see related_prs). QA harness added.
2026-03-10: Rollout plan drafted, monitoring dashboards created for 'correlation-mismatch' and duplicate-invocations metric.
Target: 2026-03-12 full rollout to Hosted and Dedicated with opt-in for Private until customer testing completes.
resolution_summary: Merged envelope_v2 encoding and parser reassembly logic. KV-cache TTL extended and CAS guard added to avoid reuse within a 10s window. Feature flag 'streaming.envelope_v2' enabled for priority customers and Dedicated fleet; observed zero duplicate tool invocations in canary traffic. Next steps: phased global rollout and compatibility shims for older clients.
postmortem_actions: Add unit + e2e test that replays proxy re-chunking patterns (flaky-net harness).
Deploy streaming.envelope_v2 by default in runtime-1.22 and require clients to support it within 30 days.
Add alert on >5 correlation-mismatch events/min per org and automated rollback if duplicates spike.
Document proxy configuration recommendations for customers (avoid aggressive buffering on L7 proxies for streaming sessions).
Schedule a session with Solutions Eng to run compatibility checks for top 20 Dedicated customers.
notes: Customer communication draft: apologetic summary, temporary mitigations steps, ETA for full fix (2026-03-12).
Security review: no PII exposure observed in misattributed payloads, but we included privacy check as part of release signoff.
